title: Euclidean boundary-immersion integral inequality and conditional flat-ball rigidity under nonnegative p-form curvature and positive (n+1-p)-curvature
author: Nicolas Ginoux; Georges Habib; Simon Raulot
work: A Poincaré Formula for Differential Forms and Applications
source_version: Official SIGMA 19 (2023) article 088, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2023.088; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The author combines harmonic extensions of exact boundary p-forms with the form-valued Reilly identity and a complete exterior-power trace computation. The equality proof then constructs a maximal family of parallel p-forms through a nontrivial rank argument using the immersion second fundamental form. This forces ambient flatness and boundary umbilicity under the stated codimension-one and connectivity restrictions, giving the full ball rigidity rather than only a numerical inequality.

source_check.note: Full Theorem3.3, supporting Theorem3.1 and the parallel-form Remark3.2 are included. The manifold is compact oriented of dimension n+1 with smooth nonempty boundary; 1<=p<=n, the Weitzenbock curvature W[p]>=0, and sigma_(n+1-p)>0 for the inward-normal convention. An isometric boundary immersion into R^(n+m) is required. The converse equality case additionally needs connected boundary, p>=2 and the immersion image contained in an (n+1)-dimensional affine subspace; the title and full source statement retain that conditional scope. Published harmonic extension/cohomology vanishing, Reilly formula and final umbilic-flat ball identification are background; the new integral reduction, boundary constancy and parallel-form rank proof are fully supplied. The sphere/hyperbolic variants are not counted separately. Source approval supplied only by exact frozen root input; no new source/difficulty decision or mathematical referee.
